acme_ops: Hey @maria_support — since last night's canary rollout (canary-2026-11-02) our order agent is getting wrong args or no tool call at all. Customers are seeing 500s because our backend expects get_order(order_id=...) but model sometimes returns call: get_order(user_id=123) or just a comment.

maria_support: Sorry to hear that — can you paste a minimal request + response and a request_id if you have one?

acme_ops: request_id=rid_9a7f3e. Example payload we send:```
POST /v1/chat/completions
{
  "model": "open-lm-2026-quant",
  "messages": [{"role":"system","content":"You are an assistant that uses tools."},{"role":"user","content":"Find order 82734 for user id 123"}],
  "functions": [{"name":"get_order","parameters":{"type":"object","properties":{"order_id":{"type":"string"}}}}],
  "function_call": "auto"
}
```

acme_ops: And the model response we got (truncated):```
{
  "id": "cmpl-xyz",
  "choices": [{
    "message": {
      "role": "assistant",
      "content": null,
      "tool_call": {
        "name": "get_order",
        "arguments": "{"user_id": 123}"
      }
    }
  }]
}
```

acme_ops: note arguments show user_id instead of order_id, so our backend fails with missing key error. Also several requests just returned a text reply: "I'll look that up" with no tool_call.

deploy-bot: Canary deployment canary-2026-11-02 completed at 1866999800. Traffic split 10% -> 100% scheduled at 1867010000 unless rollback requested.

maria_support: Thanks — assigning to infra + ML. @devon_infra can you check routing or runtime changes during the canary? @jordan_ml please check model variants / function-calling behavior.

devon_infra: I see the canary included the kernel patch that changed attention packing and a runtime tweak that optimizes tokenization for opt-architectures. No intentional changes to the functions subsystem but there was a serialization change in the assistant->tool bridge (PR #4582). Looking now at logs for rid_9a7f3e.

devon_infra: logs for rid_9a7f3e show assistant.generated_tool_call=true but bridge.transformed_args="rewrite_user_field: true" in the same microsecond. That flag was added in PR #4582 to normalize legacy payloads — might be over-aggressive.

jordan_ml: From model perspective, I ran local evals against the updated model binary used in canary. When prompt mentions both user id and order id, the model sometimes prefers user_id slot. I pushed a quick script to reproduce:```
# repro harness
> prompt = "Find order 82734 for user id 123"
> model.chat(prompt, functions=[get_order])
# sometimes returns arguments with user_id only
```
This looks like a behavior shift from the previous model checkpoint where it consistently used order_id.

maria_support: Two possible failure modes: (A) runtime rewrite accidentally maps order_id->user_id or strips the name, (B) model output tokenization changed and generation conditioning on function signature is weaker. Which seems more likely?

sam_sre: We should check canary vs baseline headers: X-model-checksum, X-runtime-version, X-function-bindings. Also check any microsecond-level reordering in the bridge. I recommend temporarily rolling canary back to 0% for this customer while we triage.

acme_ops: Can you stagger rollback for us? We have a critical flow with lots of orders queued. We can live with brief degraded throughput but not wrong args.

devon_infra: I've created a targeted rollback for acme_org (traffic -> baseline 100%) at 1867006000, should be effective now. Please confirm if you see behavior change.

acme_ops: Confirmed — next 20 calls now correctly include order_id in tool args. :thumbsup:

jordan_ml: Good. I'll run differential evals on the canary model to identify contexts where function binding drops. Also will add tightened conditioning in the prompt template and a hard constraint verifier that checks argument names before forwarding to backend.

maria_support: Thanks everyone. Action items: devon to revert the aggressive rewrite in PR #4582 and add a test for function arg name preservation; jordan to add model-level arg-name conditioning and a pre-forward validator; sam to monitor rollback and open incident if we see any delta in error rates.

acme_ops: Appreciate the quick triage — please keep us posted. We'll hold off applying any client-side workarounds.

maria_support: Filing a support ticket and tagging on-call incident channel with summary + repro. Closing thread here, will follow up in incident doc.
